key_insight: Partially applying the task vector from a non-IID batch sequence can preserve new learning while reducing forgetting better than fully integrating the update.
engineering_relevance: For continual training of engineering models on temporally clustered data, task-vector scaling offers a simple way to improve robustness across changing data regimes without rewriting the optimizer or training pipeline.
method: Compare full task-vector integration (λ=1) against partial integration with scaled vector and optimizer state.
Evaluate across continual pretraining, random-initialization pretraining, supervised post-training, and reinforcement post-training.
Test controlled streams and naturally occurring adaptation sequences, including matched learning-rate baselines.
evidence_signal: Across multiple training settings, intermediate λ values often improved average performance, and in continual-pretraining experiments task-vector scaling outperformed full integration even when the learning rate was matched.
watch_item: Benefits may depend on sequence length and distribution shift severity, so λ likely needs tuning for a given non-IID training stream.
paper_title: Task Vector Descent: Learning from Non-IID Batches
